name: Gallery-Permafrost
geological_features: Frozen canyon systems with ice-wall galleries
Glacial erratics of unusual mineral composition
specific_features: Ice walls containing preserved atmospheric samples from billions of years of history
description: Gallery-Permafrost is a large ice world whose frozen canyon systems contain layered ice walls that record the planet's atmospheric history like the pages of a geological book. The canyon walls, exposed by ancient tectonic rifting, display thousands of distinct ice layers, each representing a different epoch and each containing trapped gas bubbles that preserve the atmospheric composition of the time. The permafrost plains between canyons are patterned with polygonal fractures, their surfaces a mosaic of white and pale blue.

The thin atmosphere is bitterly cold and still, with winds rarely exceeding a gentle drift. The canyon galleries are sheltered from even this minimal air movement, creating environments of perfect stillness where ice crystals hang suspended in the air for hours. The ice walls glow faintly where sunlight penetrates, their layered structure refracting light into soft bands of white and blue that illuminate the canyon floors without warmth.

The atmospheric record preserved in the ice walls spans at least three billion years, making Gallery-Permafrost one of the most complete paleoclimatic archives ever discovered. Analysis of the trapped gas bubbles has revealed a planet that once had a thicker atmosphere and possibly liquid water, both lost to gradual atmospheric escape as the planet's magnetic field weakened. The glacial erratics scattered across the permafrost are remnants of a period of active glaciation that ended approximately one billion years ago.

Gallery-Permafrost's primary value is scientific: the ice core record is invaluable for understanding long-term atmospheric evolution and has implications for planetary engineering. The helium-3 deposits in the upper ice layers, concentrated by billions of years of solar wind implantation, are a secondary but economically meaningful resource. Strict protocols govern any activity near the canyon galleries to prevent contamination of the atmospheric record.
